moves.prompt:
You are fixing one design-system finding in the twokits repository, measured by roast-my-design-system.

The finding: Move the 12 colours written on components into the MUI theme

The detail: The most written is #667085 (9 times); Mixed1.tsx carries the most, 2, mostly #667085. #667085 is already in your theme: read it from there, from the entry that holds it in every mode. The theme in src/theme/theme.ts is where a colour is decided. On an MUI component, point at it: color: 'text.secondary' in sx, or theme.palette.primary.main in a styled() call. In the 3 files that also use Backstage UI, change only what sits on MUI components.

Expected payoff on the report's 0-100 score: about +8 points once all of them are done; fixing one file at a time lowers the count first and the score follows.

How to fix it, calmly and with respect for intent:
- A value used many times is a decision without a name, not a mistake. Name it and consolidate; never blind-delete.
- Small pixel nudges and one-off layout widths can be deliberate craft. Keep the deliberate exceptions; round the accidents to a neighbouring step.
- Prefer the tokens, scale steps and canonical components this repository already has over inventing new ones.
- Keep every change mechanical and reviewable. No redesigns, no drive-by refactors, no renamed files unless the finding asks for it.
- A chart series, an illustration or a status colour keeps its colour. Add it to the theme palette under a name rather than swapping it to a grey.
- Before pointing a colour at a theme entry, check the entry has that value in every mode. A dark-mode text colour used on a surface that is dark in both modes needs its own fixed entry, not the mode-aware one.
- A colour that identifies someone else's service stays where it is: an integration's brand colour, a provider's badge, a logo. Tokenise the colours your own interface uses.
- Read the theme where the kit reads it: sx paths ('text.secondary', 'primary.main'), theme.palette in styled() and makeStyles. Never import the theme file into a component just to read a hex.
- This repo also uses Backstage UI (@backstage/ui). Make these changes only on MUI components and the wrappers around them. On Backstage UI components, style them the way the files around them do; sx, styled() and the MUI theme do not reach them.

Work through the files named in the finding. When you are done, re-run the scan to verify the payoff:

npx roast-my-design-system@latest

The finding: Put the 13 pixel spacings on the theme's spacing steps

The detail: The most written is p: 12px (6 times); Mixed1.tsx carries the most, 3, mostly p: 20px. MUI spacing is a step count: p: 2 is theme.spacing(2), which is 8px on this theme (one step is 4px). A spacing that lands exactly on a step becomes the step; one that does not stays. In the 3 files that also use Backstage UI, change only what sits on MUI components.

Expected payoff on the report's 0-100 score: about +8 points once all of them are done; fixing one file at a time lowers the count first and the score follows.

How to fix it, calmly and with respect for intent:
- A value used many times is a decision without a name, not a mistake. Name it and consolidate; never blind-delete.

- Prefer the tokens, scale steps and canonical components this repository already has over inventing new ones.
- Keep every change mechanical and reviewable. No redesigns, no drive-by refactors, no renamed files unless the finding asks for it.
- Convert a spacing only when it lands exactly on one of this theme's steps. A size between steps is a decision: leave it and say so.
- Only padding, margin and gap. Font size and line height belong to typography variants, radius to the theme's shape; a bare number for lineHeight is a multiplier, not pixels.
- Never touch width, height or a size another element depends on.
- A bare number is a spacing step only inside sx and theme.spacing(). Inside style={{}} or a plain style object it is pixels, so convert only in sx.
- This repo also uses Backstage UI (@backstage/ui). Make these changes only on MUI components and the wrappers around them. On Backstage UI components, style them the way the files around them do; sx, styled() and the MUI theme do not reach them.
